public_rationale: OpenAI documents adoption growth through May 2025 [e1]. Microsoft reported over half a billion Bing chats since its February launch by May 8, 2023 [e2]. An evaluation revised August 4, 2025 found 5%–13% of responses unsafe across four chatbots, documenting repeated deficient advice [e3]. A clinical preprint examined records from December 1, 2022 through April 1, 2026 and identified 28 patients with psychosis-worsening AI interactions [e4]. This supports mental-health harm, though missing conversation logs limit attribution [e4]. The August 14, 2025 bromism report describes physical injury following alleged chatbot advice, but lacks the original logs and a calendar date for the injury [e5]. The evidence does not establish the dated, attributable physical injury required to resolve the forecast as supported [e5].
limitations: The Bing total covers use since February 2023 and does not isolate growth after the April 4 forecast [e2].
The advice evaluation measures potential harm in tested responses, not population rates of deficient advice or actual injury [e3].
The retrospective mental-health preprint lacks conversation logs and cannot fully separate chatbot contribution from competing causes [e4].
The physical-injury report does not verify the original advice or date the clinical event [e5].

our_interpretation: Growth in chatbot and chat-based-search use is an antecedent, not merely background.
Read a lot as repeated, non-isolated materially deficient advice; no numerical prevalence threshold is supplied.
Read the health statement as predicting actual injuries attributable at least partly to deficient advice or guidance, including exacerbation of existing illness.
Both mental and physical health are included. Potentially harmful answers alone do not establish actual injury.
Clinical evidence may establish contribution without proving that chatbot use was the sole cause. Allegations or temporal association alone are insufficient.
criteria.support_condition: After adoption grows, repeated materially deficient advice is documented and credible clinical or equivalent records establish actual mental and physical injury to which that advice contributed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive event permanently rules out the predicted outcomes under the stated condition. A finite period without documented injury cannot falsify this forecast without a deadline.
